entries.workflow: Application shell, navigation, search, and unavailable routes

decisions.after: Search this workspace
decisions.reason: Search is limited to the active workspace, not the whole installation.

decisions.after: Available areas
decisions.reason: Area is a familiar navigation term; capability is product-contract language.

decisions.after: Staff and invitations
decisions.reason: Use ordinary prose instead of a compact navigation abbreviation.

decisions.before: Find records you are authorized to view in the active workspace.
decisions.after: Find documents and records in this workspace.
decisions.reason: Authorization is enforced automatically and does not need to be narrated.

decisions.before: No authorized records match this search.
decisions.after: No records match this search.
decisions.reason: The shorter empty state describes the result without implementation language.

entries.workflow: First-owner setup, sign-in, MFA, account invitations, password recovery, profile, sessions, and API tokens

decisions.after: Use your TekDocs account.
decisions.reason: Invited staff and administrators use the same sign-in screen; the old text incorrectly implied that only owners could sign in.

decisions.before: The browser could not confirm the installation or session state.
decisions.after: TekDocs could not load your sign-in status.
decisions.reason: Describe what the person needs to know without exposing browser or session-state implementation details.

decisions.after: Setup token
decisions.reason: Setup token describes why the value is needed while the nearby instructions retain the exact server commands.

decisions.before: If that address belongs to an active account, a password reset link has been sent. The same message is shown for every address.
decisions.after: If an active account uses that address, we sent a password reset link.
decisions.reason: Keep the enumeration-safe response without explaining the security implementation to the person signing in.

decisions.after: Sign out
decisions.reason: A person is ending a browser session; sign out is the familiar action and states the outcome.

decisions.after: Create token
decisions.reason: Create is ordinary product language; issue is unnecessary credential-management jargon.

entries.workflow: Staff administration, access control, email delivery administration, and system diagnostics

decisions.before: Invite MSP staff, review account activation, and hand accepted members into access control.
decisions.after: Invite staff, see who has joined, and manage invitations.
decisions.reason: Describe the work available on the page instead of narrating the application workflow.

decisions.before: Tenant roles apply only where the organization access mode also allows the member.
decisions.after: A role controls what a staff member can do. Client access controls where they can do it.
decisions.reason: Separate role and client access concepts in language an MSP owner can act on.

decisions.after: Always has access
decisions.reason: State the owner's access outcome without exposing installation terminology.

decisions.after: Client access
decisions.reason: The product consistently presents managed organizations as clients in MSP workflows.

decisions.after: Failed
decisions.reason: Operators need the actionable delivery state; the queue implementation term does not help them retry an email.

decisions.after: Diagram service
decisions.reason: Service describes what the operator is checking while exact failure codes and the package version remain available for diagnosis.

entries.workflow: Organizations, people, sites, and custom fields

decisions.after: Organization types
decisions.reason: Type is the familiar term for choosing whether an organization is a client, vendor, manufacturer, or partner.

decisions.after: This person is listed in {workspace}.
decisions.reason: Describe the visible result without exposing the association model.

decisions.after: Saved site / Saved location
decisions.reason: Saved distinguishes reusable site records from retained text without implementation language.

decisions.before: Location label / Office label · Retained fallback text
decisions.after: Site name / Location name · Kept if the saved record is later archived
decisions.reason: Explain why the text is stored and when it remains useful.

decisions.after: Field key · Used by imports and integrations; cannot be changed later
decisions.reason: Name the value plainly and explain the consequence at the decision point.

decisions.before: Inherited from MSP / Managed by MSP
decisions.after: From MSP workspace / Edit from MSP workspace
decisions.reason: Tell staff where the field comes from and where it can be changed.

decisions.before: Version created. N existing values remain compatible; N require review.
decisions.after: New version created. N existing values are still valid; N need review. No values were changed. (Singular counts use singular grammar.)
decisions.reason: Replace migration terminology while preserving the exact impact and safety guarantee.

entries.workflow: Documents, templates, structured types, settings, review, publication, files, and exports

decisions.after: Publish document / locked copy that cannot be edited
decisions.reason: Publication is the stable product term; storage and immutability details are explained only where they affect the decision.

decisions.before: MSP client templates with live, pinned, or independent references
decisions.after: Templates from your MSP with Copy once, Keep updated, or Keep this version
decisions.reason: The choices now describe what happens to the client's content when the template changes.

decisions.after: Who can see it? MSP staff / Client portal
decisions.reason: The options name the people and destination directly.

decisions.before: Export editable snapshot and portable bundle manifest
decisions.after: Download editable copy and Download ZIP
decisions.reason: The UI distinguishes editable downloads from a published version without exposing package internals.

decisions.after: Documents that will update or keep their current version
decisions.reason: Impact is stated as an outcome for each affected document.

decisions.after: Document files and Create document
decisions.reason: Files remain attached to documents; implementation-specific storage terms do not help complete the task.

decisions.after: Web source
decisions.reason: The workflow checks a public web page and lets the user review changes before applying them.

entries.workflow: Assets, licenses, networks, domains, certificates, credentials, and services

decisions.before: Provenance checksum / Retained specifications / STATIC product documentation
decisions.after: Source check / Saved specifications / Published product documents
decisions.reason: Keep the supplier record verifiable while naming the information and documents the technician can actually use.

decisions.before: New asset from supplier model / applicable STATIC publications will be retained
decisions.after: New asset / current specifications and published product documents will be copied into the asset record
decisions.reason: Explain what the supplier-model choice does without exposing publication modes or storage language.

decisions.before: Choose a license to inspect its entitlement / Revoke seat
decisions.after: Choose a license to view its details / Unassign seat
decisions.reason: Details and unassign describe the ordinary task; entitlement and revoke are unnecessary licensing jargon here.

decisions.before: Credential references / 1Password remains the security boundary / handoff
decisions.after: Credential links / Credentials stay in 1Password / Open in 1Password
decisions.reason: Tell staff what TekDocs stores, where the credential remains, and what the action does without narrating the security architecture.

decisions.before: Monitoring details / Collection history / retained monitoring evidence
decisions.after: Domain checks / Check history / Previous checks
decisions.reason: Checks are the visible operation; source-specific RDAP, DNS, DNSSEC, CAA, and TLS terms remain because technicians need their exact meaning.

decisions.after: Result ID
decisions.reason: The displayed digest identifies a saved check result; Evidence overstated what the shortened value alone represented.

decisions.before: Commercial records / operational fields with a separate access policy
decisions.after: Services and contracts / Staff need permission to view Costs
decisions.reason: Name the records and the actual visibility consequence at the form where pricing is separated.

decisions.after: A vendor sells a product; a manufacturer makes it; an organization can be both
decisions.reason: Explain the classification distinction once where staff choose or review a supplier catalog.

decisions.before: Suppliers derived from retained asset provenance
decisions.after: Vendors and manufacturers connected to this workspace’s assets
decisions.reason: Describe why an organization appears in the list without exposing storage or lineage terminology.

decisions.before: Specification sets / reusable validation contracts / checksum
decisions.after: Specification templates / details recorded for a model
decisions.reason: A template describes the task directly; the unlabeled checksum is hidden because it does not help an ordinary catalog decision.

decisions.after: Update model / change notes / Save new version
decisions.reason: Use familiar actions while still stating that a saved update creates a new version and does not rewrite existing assets.

decisions.after: Published document / Add document / documents included with assets
decisions.reason: Name the document and the result of linking it instead of exposing publication-mode and relationship terminology.

decisions.after: Product and models leave new-asset choices; existing assets keep saved details; no restore action is available
decisions.reason: The confirmation names the full consequence before an archive that the current interface cannot reverse.

entries.workflow: Invoice settings, drafts, issuance, delivery, lifecycle, and accounting handoff

decisions.after: Items / price per unit / enter an item manually
decisions.reason: Use the terms an MSP expects while building an invoice instead of accounting record terminology.

decisions.before: Browser confirmation for issue or delete
decisions.after: In-page confirmation naming the draft date and permanent consequence
decisions.reason: Keep the decision visible, accessible, and specific before assigning a permanent number or deleting a draft.

decisions.after: Status / accounting / sent to accounting
decisions.reason: Describe what happened to the invoice without requiring bookkeeping-system vocabulary.

decisions.before: Provider event ID / external record ID
decisions.after: Unique update ID / invoice ID in accounting system
decisions.reason: Name the values by the job they do and explain that the update ID prevents duplicates.

decisions.before: Invoice settings could not be saved
decisions.after: Couldn't save invoice settings; changes remain; try again
decisions.reason: Failure messages state what happened, whether work was preserved, and the next action.

decisions.after: Issued and locked with a verification ID
decisions.reason: Keep useful proof visible without making ordinary invoice readers interpret a cryptographic algorithm.

entries.workflow: MSP supplies, purchasing references, quantity changes, client use, and invoice pricing

decisions.after: Stock
decisions.reason: Stock is the familiar name for supplies the MSP keeps on hand and distinguishes them from client assets.

decisions.after: Adjust stock
decisions.reason: The action records what physically happened without introducing accounting terminology.

decisions.after: Used at client
decisions.reason: The option says where the material went and prompts for the client only when needed.

entries.workflow: Taxonomies, compliance, reminders, activity, and recycle bin

decisions.before: Managed vocabularies used for consistent document metadata across every client.
decisions.after: A taxonomy is a shared list of terms used to organize documents consistently.
decisions.reason: Defines the unfamiliar term once, where a user decides whether to create one.

decisions.after: Match existing tags / Preview matches
decisions.reason: Describes the user’s task instead of the underlying data operation.

decisions.before: Versioned control catalogs, applicability decisions, accountable owners, and retained review history for this workspace.
decisions.after: Track compliance controls, evidence, and risks for this workspace.
decisions.reason: Keeps necessary compliance terms while removing implementation language.

decisions.before: Create signed bundle / Immutable signed snapshots of the current controls, evidence, and risks.
decisions.after: Create locked bundle / Locked copies of the current controls, evidence, and risks.
decisions.reason: Explains the result without requiring knowledge of signing or storage details.

decisions.before: Permission-aware, append-only changes in the active workspace.
decisions.after: See changes made in this workspace.
decisions.reason: Leaves audit implementation details out of the ordinary page introduction.

decisions.before: This also restores records archived in the same cascade.
decisions.after: This also restores related records that were archived with it.
decisions.reason: States the consequence in language a user can act on.

entries.workflow: Integrations, imports, webhooks, synchronization, observations, conflicts, and recovery
entries.next_review: Replace provider and synchronization implementation terms in ordinary setup while preserving precise audit codes in technical logs.

entries.workflow: Client portal documents, publications, files, and invoices
entries.next_review: Review client-facing publication and invoice language without exposing internal storage, authorization, or provider terms.
